### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2c9891be406c1bbe86cd5a4765b6149f15982c7b` — the merge of head `29af940fde182fd480eb8c328f34b9e597e452a3` into base `5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2c9891be406c1bbe86cd5a4765b6149f15982c7b && git checkout 2c9891be406c1bbe86cd5a4765b6149f15982c7b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613 29af940fde182fd480eb8c328f34b9e597e452a3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613 && git merge --no-ff 29af940fde182fd480eb8c328f34b9e597e452a3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `29af940fde182fd480eb8c328f34b9e597e452a3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/data/currency-config-home-amount.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (`readonly` / `expression` field keys, read), content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx, content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx, content/docs/references/data/field.mdx (the `homeAmount` prose, read for drift)

Inputs: card #28205 body and its five comments (triage p3, unblocked, `pm:queue`, the seat claim, the os-dev-report); PR #29533 body, file list (3 files, +32/-6) and `git diff origin/main...29af940f`; the check-runs on `29af940f`. Judged against the live tree, not the PR body.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set — unchanged, right.** On `main` the early return is `t?.readonly === true && t.expression === undefined`. On the head it is `!writable && !computed` with `writable = t?.readonly !== true` and `computed = t?.expression !== undefined`; `!writable` is `t?.readonly === true` and `!computed` is `t?.expression === undefined`, so the return condition is the same predicate on the same inputs. `FieldSchema.readonly` is `z.boolean().default(false)` (field.zod.ts:2371), so a parsed field never has `readonly: undefined`; even if it did, both forms treat it as writable. Every object accepted on `main` is accepted on the head and vice versa. `Clause-②: no` holds.
- **Single-fault messages — byte-identical, right.** Old `readonly === true` branch: `'declares an `expression`, so the engine would store a second, computed value in the same column. ' + 'Delete `expression` from `T`.'`; new `!writable` branch: `${computedFault}. Delete `expression` from `T`.` with `computedFault` the same text minus the trailing `. ` — the concatenation is the same string. Old else branch and the new `writable`-only branch likewise. The existing two `it.each` refusals (`without readonly: true`, `declaring an expression`) still hold without edit.
- **Both-faults message — new text, right.** The only observable change: a target with `readonly !== true` AND an `expression` now receives one issue, same `code: 'custom'`, same path `fields.AMOUNT.currencyConfig.homeAmount.field|rateField`, whose message names both faults and both remedies ("Add `readonly: true` to `T` and delete its `expression`."). Issue count at that pointer stays one; no second pointer gains or loses an issue. The call sites (object.zod.ts:2094 `'the home field'`, :2148 `'the rate field'`) are unchanged, so the refusal still fires only after existence, type, mode and ownership checks pass for that target — exactly where it fired before.
- **Public surface — none moved.** No export, schema key, accepted value, generated artifact or docs anchor changes; `git grep` of both message fragments on `main` outside object.zod.ts returns nothing, so no snapshot or docs page pins the old text.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28205-home-amount-both-faults.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. A refusal-message text change with an unchanged accept set is a patch; `Clause-②: no` is correct per ① (nothing accepted on `main` is refused on the head, and nothing refused is accepted). The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. Not a `(narrowing)` arm; no `!` in the title. Matches what the diff publishes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `out_of_scope_findings: []` — nothing to answer.
- Dev flag "Human Minimum 3 unchecked: `pnpm lint` not run locally" — left to CI; `Lint · ESLint` is `in_progress` at review time (see below). Not a code finding.
- Dev flag "two merges of origin/main" — the head `29af940f` is a merge commit; the three-dot diff against `origin/main` is exactly the three intended files, so the merges carried nothing of their own. `main` has moved since (unrelated changesets only); neither scoped code file changed on `main` after the merge-base, so no conflict and no stale premise.
- Check-runs on `29af940f` at review time: concluded — `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Auto Label`, `filter` all `success`; the opt-in / schedule / UI-artifact jobs `skipped`. Still `in_progress` — `Build Core`, `Build UI Deps`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Live E2E UI`, `Check Changeset`, `Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger`, `Lint · ESLint / CI, release & engine gates / repo & tooling gates / docs & code guards / scoped · slot lookup & corpus / scoped · query-options erasure`. No concluded run failed. The verdict below is on the concluded runs plus the read of the tree; the spec test and typecheck legs have not yet concluded in CI (the dev reports 792 files / 23524 tests green and typecheck exit 0 locally on this head, which this record does not adopt as a gate verdict). If any in-progress run concludes red, the merge gate — not this record — holds it.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts** — judged against the card's ruling (triage: "one refusal names both faults", p3), ADR-0144 D5 as the test file cites it, and the first consumer (`os validate` / any object save through `ObjectSchema.safeParse`).

- Holds. The ruling wants both faults and both remedies in one issue at the existing pointer; the head does exactly that and nothing else. I tried to break it:
  - Could `writable && computed` fire where neither single fault fired before? No — it is reachable only past the same early return, so every refusal on the head is a refusal on `main`.
  - Could the both-faults branch shadow a single fault? No — `writable` alone and `!writable` (hence `computed`) alone fall through to the two old strings; the ternary is exhaustive over the three reachable states.
  - Does the longer sentence still lead with the pointer and end with the prescription, as the sibling refusals do? Yes: "`amount.currencyConfig.homeAmount.field` names `amount_home`, the home field only the engine writes, but it does not declare `readonly: true`, so … , and it declares an `expression`, so … . Add `readonly: true` to `amount_home` and delete its `expression`." Consistent with the refusal style of the rest of `refuseDishonestHomeAmount`.
  - Rate-field path: the rate holder is judged once (the first holder, `holder === undefined` branch) as before; a second amount sharing a consistent rate field is still not re-judged. Unchanged.
- **Test** (`currency-config-home-amount.test.ts`): the new `it.each` over `amount_home` / `amount_rate` overrides `BASE_FIELDS[name]` with `readonly: false, expression: 'record.amount'`, asserts one issue at the pointer, `code: custom`, both fault fragments and the joint remedy — the one pinned case the card asked for, placed beside the two single-fault cases it extends. `expression` on a non-formula `currency` / `number` field is already accepted by the field schema (the existing `declaring an expression` case relies on it), so the case exercises the refinement and not a field-level refusal. Assertions use `toContain` like their neighbours rather than the exact string; acceptable, and the joint-remedy fragment is specific enough that the single-fault branches cannot satisfy it (the dev's ablation — both-faults condition to `false` — reports exactly these 2 cases failing, which is the expected shape).
- **Docs** (read, not reviewed): the three `homeAmount` prose rows describe the rule (`readonly: true`, engine-written) and do not quote the refusal text, so no drift.
- Findings: no must-fix. No should-fix.
